position: CDC (relationship with the CDC Foundation); NIH (relationship with the Foundation for the NIH)
proposal: The Mandate recommends banning the CDC from accepting pharmaceutical industry contributions through the CDC Foundation, a route it describes as a loophole used since 1992 (p. 454), and decommissioning the CDC and NIH Foundations so that private donations, a majority of them from drug companies, cannot influence research funding or public health policy (p. 462). It also states a broader goal of keeping CDC, NIH and FDA regulators free of private biopharmaceutical funding (p. 452).
remaining: A ban on CDC acceptance of pharmaceutical industry contributions through the CDC Foundation (p. 454)
Decommissioning of the CDC Foundation and the NIH Foundation (p. 462)
Funding of CDC, NIH and FDA directly from government appropriations rather than private biopharmaceutical sources (p. 452)

review.mandate_note: Per the record's pages and proposal fields (pp. 452, 454, 462), the Mandate asks that CDC be barred from taking pharmaceutical industry money through the CDC Foundation and that the CDC and NIH Foundations be decommissioned, as part of a goal of keeping health regulators free of drug-industry funding. The chapter text was not available to this review.

uncertainties: No action since 2025-01-20 bars CDC from accepting pharmaceutical money through the CDC Foundation or decommissions the CDC Foundation or the Foundation for the NIH.
